## 🔴🔴 `check_layer_echo.py` MEASURES THE SOURCES TRAILER AS PART OF "KEY TAKEAWAYS" — THE WORKLIST THIS WAVE WAS BUILT FROM IS PARTLY AN ARTEFACT

**Found by the `switching_positions.md` agent, which refused to accept its own headline figure and went and read the
tool.** ✅ **VERIFIED BY THE COORDINATOR against `scripts/check_layer_echo.py`.**

**`_layers()` slices from a `## ` heading to the NEXT `## ` heading — `end = heads[n+1][0] if n+1 < len(heads)
else len(lines)`.** ⚠️⚠️ **For the LAST `## ` heading, `end` is EOF. The Sources trailer in this corpus HAS
NO HEADING. So wherever `## Key Takeaways` is the last heading, its "layer" is the ten takeaways PLUS THE WHOLE
TRAILER** — which quotes the same rulebook text Common Mistakes quotes.

**MEASURED, corpus-wide:**

| | |
|---|---|
| documents where `## Key Takeaways` is the LAST `##` heading | **37 of 39** |
| trailer words swept into the "Key Takeaways" layer | **226,228** |

| trailer wds | "KT layer" wds | document | trailer share |
|---:|---:|---|---:|
| 14,228 | 18,604 | `body_contact_and_battles.md` | **76%** |
| 13,577 | 17,138 | `goaltender.md` | **79%** |
| 12,808 | 18,409 | `rules_primer.md` | **70%** |
| 9,910 | 11,183 | `shooting.md` | **89%** |
| 9,477 | 11,076 | `special_teams.md` | **86%** |

**The agent measured its own document both ways.** Shingles shared between Common Mistakes and the **actual** Key
Takeaways: **94 at HEAD → 8 after its work** (11.8% → 1.3%). **The 10.3% the tool still reports is the trailer,
which is provenance and MUST NOT BE CUT.**

⚠️⚠️ **AND CLAUDE.MD'S OWN SENTENCE IS AN INSTANCE OF IT:** *"`check_layer_echo.py` scored
`switching_positions.md`'s Common Mistakes → Key Takeaways at **20.1%**, which is what a duplicate looks like."*
**That figure is KT + trailer, not KT.**

### ⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT INVALIDATE
❌ **It does NOT invalidate the wave.** The duplication the agents found was **real and literal** —
`practice_and_development.md`'s Overview paragraphs `:31–:41` **were the same sentences** as KT1–KT4;
`scanning_and_anticipation.md`'s Overview was a second kernel list. **Those are not trailer artefacts.**
✅ **What it invalidates is the RANKING.** Documents were ordered partly by **how long their Sources trailer is**.
⚠️ **A document with a short trailer and real duplication could sit below the cut.**

🔴 **THIS IS THE FOURTH TIME THIS SESSION A COORDINATOR WORKLIST OVER-COUNTED** — after 707 flow-breaking
callouts (real panels: 4), 228 bare closed counts (wrong in BOTH directions on two files), and the chunk baseline
that compared a file to itself. **The pattern is not carelessness about arithmetic: it is trusting a tool's headline
number without reading what the tool counts.** ✅ **Every one of the four was caught by an AGENT, not by me.**

### ⚠️ NOT FIXED YET, AND DELIBERATELY SO
**`scripts/` is shared state and THREE AGENTS ARE LIVE ON IT.** CLAUDE.md: *"Change a tool between waves, not during
one."* **Round 59's recorded failure is a classifier changed mid-round, after which *"no finding in any report
should rest on that tool's output today."*** → **Fix `_layers()` to stop the last layer at the trailer BETWEEN
waves, then re-measure the corpus and rebuild the worklist.**

**Several agents independently named cross-document divergence as their blind spot, and the USA Hockey 620 finding
came from exactly it. So I tested whether the corpus's existing tool covers it. IT DOES NOT.**

**The tool keys on the RULE NUMBER AS WRITTEN.** Measured:
- **`620(a)`** appears as a key — **5 units, *"spread 1"*, which reads as CLEAN.**
- **`620(c)` NEVER APPEARS AS A KEY AT ALL.**

⚠️⚠️ **`passing_and_receiving.md` cites 620(a); `body_contact_and_battles.md` cites 620(c). DIFFERENT SUB-CLAUSES
OF ONE RULE ARE DIFFERENT KEYS — so the two documents disagreeing about whether USA Hockey's head-contact ceiling is
a game misconduct or a MATCH PENALTY scores as two separate, internally consistent entries.**
⚠️ **And the tool measures BOOK SETS, not TARIFFS.** **Two documents can name identical book sets and state
opposite ceilings, and it reports them as agreeing.**

⚠️ **NO FIX IS PROPOSED HERE, and this is NOT a row to sweep.** **CLAUDE.md: the tool has no `--strict` and never
will — *"a site naming one book because it discusses one book is correct, and a tool that ranked these and then
offered to fix them is precisely how round 44 manufactured a divergence that did not exist."*** **It currently
reports 284 rule numbers with mixed scope, which is calibration noise.** ✅ **The finding is the GAP, recorded so
nobody mistakes a clean `check_rule_scope` run for evidence that the corpus agrees with itself about a tariff.**

   Hockey games and practices until their case has been dealt with**"*, hearing *"within 30 days"*, and the
   Discipline Policy lists ***"Rule 615(c) Fighting (Helmet Removal)"* at Level 3 — *"a recommended range of a
   3-5 game suspension."*** ⚠️ **The document prices it as *"it ends your game."* The reader is told the bill is
   settled at the final buzzer.**

   both.** **Hockey Canada writes it too at 10.6(f)(iv), a gross misconduct, sitting immediately below the

## ✅ A DECLARED PERMISSIVE RISK, RESOLVED BY THE COORDINATOR — AND IT RESOLVES SAFE

**The `team_play_and_culture.md` agent wrote around a heading rather than assert it, and asked for a `pdftoppm`
read:** ***"`hc.txt`/`hc_layout.txt` Interpretation 6's heading prints **'Rule 7.10 (d)'**, not (e). If it is the
book's own, the interpretation may attach to 7.10(d) — the RETURN-TO-BENCH misconduct — rather than to the
peacemaker clause, and my scope sentence would be wrong in the PERMISSIVE direction."***

⚠️ **No Hockey Canada PDF is on disk, so `pdftoppm` was not available.** ✅ **But TWO INDEPENDENT EXTRACTIONS
are — `hc.txt` and the layout-preserving `hc_layout.txt` — and BOTH print `Interpretation 6 Rule 7.10 (d)`
IDENTICALLY. So it is the BOOK'S OWN HEADING, not an extraction artefact.**

✅ **RESOLVED BY READING THE CLAUSE LIST (`hc_layout.txt:5138`):**
- **7.10 (d)** — *"A **Misconduct** penalty will be assessed to any player who, when a fight occurs, **does not
  immediately return to their respective benches**…"*
- **7.10 (e)** — *"A **Game Misconduct** penalty will be assessed to a player who: … ii. **joins in a fight or acts
  as a peacemaker**…"*

🔴 **So the heading is a TYPO IN THE BOOK.** **Interpretation 6's own text names *"a player who acts as a
peacemaker"*, which is 7.10(e)(ii), not (d).**

✅✅ **AND THE WORRY DISSOLVES COMPLETELY, BECAUSE 7.10(d) CARRIES ITS OWN NOTE 1 SAYING THE SAME THING:**
> ***"Note 1: In order to apply this rule, **at least one player must be assessed a Major penalty and Game
> Misconduct penalty for Fighting**."***

**BOTH clauses are fight-scoped — (d) by its own Note 1, (e) by Interpretation 6 — so the fight-scope the repair
wrote is CORRECT EITHER WAY, and there is no permissive reading available.**
✅ **The agent's judgement to cite it as *"its Interpretation 6"* WITHOUT a sub-clause was exactly right: it
avoided asserting a heading it could not verify, and the citation is true under both readings.**

⚠️ **RECORDED FOR THE NEXT READER: `hc.txt` and `hc_layout.txt` both print Interpretation 6 under a heading that
contradicts its own text. Do not "correct" the corpus to 7.10(d).** **Same family as the `carha.txt` dangling
*"Rule 86(d)"* cross-reference found earlier today — a defect IN THE BOOK, not in the corpus.**

REGARDLESS.** ⚠️ **CLAUDE.md does not draw that distinction, and I applied a mid-paragraph rule to a
paragraph-initial case.** **My edit would have been a rendering NO-OP that merely un-bolded a glyph inside an

## 🔴🔴 A RETRACTION — MY "THIRTY-SECOND ERROR" WAS NOT AN ERROR, AND RECORDING IT WOULD HAVE DAMAGED CORRECT TEXT

⚠️⚠️ **I logged *"USA Hockey 618(a) for the Note to 625(b)"* as a failed coordinator claim. A fourth `commit-gate`
read BOTH rules and refuted me: BOTH NOTES EXIST AND BOTH ARE REAL.**
- **618(a) Note** — *"**For the purpose of this rule**, the goal crease shall extend from the ice to the top of the
  crossbar of the goal frame."*
- **625(b) Note** — *"The goal crease area shall include all the space outlined by the semi-circular crease lines
  (including crease lines) and extending vertically to the level of the top of the goal frame."*

✅ **SAME HEIGHT, DIFFERENT SCOPE. `center.md`'s 625(b) is right for a SCREENING/INTERFERENCE section;
`puck_handling.md`'s 618(a) is right for a HANDLING-THE-PUCK section. NEITHER FILE IS WRONG.**
🔴🔴 **THE GATE'S WARNING IS THE WHOLE POINT: *"a future agent told '618(a) is the error' WILL DAMAGE CORRECT
TEXT."*** ⚠️⚠️ **A FALSE ENTRY IN AN ERROR LOG IS A LOADED WEAPON — this file's error list is read as settled fact by
every brief, and I nearly armed one that would have rewritten two correct citations.** **The agent that reported it
to me was right about ITS OWN file and I over-generalised its finding into a corpus-wide rule. THAT was the error.**

### ⚠️ THE REAL NIT IS THE OPPOSITE ONE, AND IT IS A D4 POINT

## 🔴🔴 CLAUDE.md'S OWN "FOURTH STATE" GUIDANCE WAS **WRONG**, AND IT NEARLY CAUSED CORPUS-WIDE CHURN

⚠️⚠️ **A `commit-gate` read CLAUDE.md, inferred a POSITION rule, and briefed a repair for a CORRECT line. An agent
REFUSED IT and proved the premise false.**
**CLAUDE.md said:** *"`markInlineWarnings` needs the glyph to **PRECEDE** a strong run — it reads the *preceding text
node*. A glyph **within** the bold gets the bold and nothing else."*
🔴 **THAT NAMES ONLY SHAPE (b). `markInlineWarnings` HANDLES THREE SHAPES AND ITS OWN COMMENTS NAME THEM.**
**`WARNING_LEAD_RE` — `/^\s*(\d+[.)]\s*)?(⚠|❗|🚫)/u` — is tested against THE STRONG RUN'S OWN TEXT and is checked
FIRST, before any preceding node is looked at.**
✅ **SO `**⚠️ text**` IS WRAPPED WHEREVER THE RUN SITS IN THE PARAGRAPH.**

### ✅ THE REAL DISCRIMINATOR, AND IT IS NOT POSITION
🔴 **It is whether the glyph LEADS the strong run.**
- `**⚠️ text**` → **shape (a), wrapped.** ✅ **Fine anywhere.**
- `**head, ⚠️ hazard.**` → **untreated.** 🔴 **This is the genuine fourth state, and the close-and-reopen repair is
  still right for it.**
⚠️⚠️ **THE GATE'S RULE — *"mid-paragraph → move the glyph out; paragraph-opening → leave it alone"* — IS WRONG AND
WOULD HAVE CAUSED CHURN ACROSS THE CORPUS.** ⚠️ **Its sibling check on `defender.md`'s trapezoid paragraph came out
CORRECT FOR THE WRONG REASON — that line is fine because the glyph LEADS the run, not because the paragraph opens
with it.**

1. **Source** — `WARNING_LEAD_RE` read in `remark-corpus.mjs` with the comment block naming shapes (a), (b) and (c).
2. **BUILT HTML, corpus-wide** — every `index.html` scanned for `<strong>` runs opening with a warning glyph:
   **80 found, EVERY ONE either `warn-inline`-wrapped or inside a `callout-warning` aside. ZERO UNTREATED.**
✅ **AND IT DID NOT MAKE THE EDIT: *"Had I made it, `⚠️ **Hockey Canada says…**` would be shape (b) — also
`warn-inline`. Identical render, identical spoken output. A ZERO-VALUE EDIT MADE ON A FALSE PREMISE."***
✅ **Census of all six `⚠️`-in-`<strong>` runs in `center.md`: ALL SIX are shape (a). The inverse search for the real
state-4 shape returns ZERO hits in that file.**
✅ **CLAUDE.md CORRECTED at both sites.** ⚠️ **The *"63 of 76 wrapped"* figure already in that passage was ALWAYS
shape (a) working — the number was right and the explanation beside it was wrong.**

## 🔴🔴 THREE CORPUS-WIDE FINDINGS FROM THIS WAVE

### 1. THE PWHL OFFSET IS **NOT CONSTANT**
**Interference shifts +1 (NHL 56 → PWHL 57). Later rules shift +2 (63→65, 81→83, 69→71).** ⚠️ **PWHL 56.1 is
HOOKING.** 🔴 ***"NEVER DERIVE A PWHL NUMBER — LOOK IT UP."*** ⚠️ **My own briefs have been treating the offset as
uniform. It is not.**
✅ **And the agent reported a NEGATIVE it nearly filed as a finding: it went hunting for a `76`-for-faceoffs error on
the strength of the shifting offset and there was none — the `76.5` sites are a genuinely different rule.**

### 2. THE DISCLOSED-INSERTION CONVENTION PROTECTS THE READER AND NOT THE LISTENER
🔴 **`[your]` speaks as plain *"your"*, attributed to books that say *his*, *their* and *her*.** ⚠️ **Still a NET GAIN
here, because `[the]` was ambiguous in the DANGEROUS direction — but it is *"a gain inside a convention that protects
the reader and not the listener, corpus-wide, and NO CHECKER SEES IT."***
✅ **The proposed remedy: *"books as subject is the only form that survives the renderer."*** 🔴 **Routed to
`safety-reviewer` for a view, because it bears on EVERY disclosed insertion in the corpus.**

### 3. 🔴 THE DISCRIMINATOR FOR THE HARSHER-SIMPLER SHAPE — **THE CLOSED QUANTIFIER**
> ***"The discriminator between Items 1 and 2 is the CLOSED QUANTIFIER, and that is the whole difference."***
- **`faceoffs.md` KT2 said *"all five"* — a CLOSED quantifier — so dropping a condition made it CONTRADICT its own
  facts line. REPAIRED.**
- **`center.md` KT9 carries NO quantifier and no book closure, so it is SHORTER THAN the body, not CONTRARY to it.
  LEFT, and the agent concurred with the three previous declines.**
✅ **THIS IS THE TEST I HAVE BEEN APPLYING BY INSTINCT ALL SESSION, NOW STATED: does the sentence CLOSE a quantifier
over the books? If yes it must be exact. If no, shorter is legitimate.**

**was real, two hops out.**

word REMOVED from its own context window, then filtered to units that instruct **body contact or body

## 🔴🔴 A PREMISE THIS COORDINATOR SHIPPED IN EVERY BRIEF TODAY IS WRONG: KEY TAKEAWAYS ARE **PACKED**, NOT EACH VOICED ALONE

**Measured by an agent on `goaltender.md` and RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY by the coordinator on
`defender.md`, 25 September 2026.**

**`goaltender.md`, 231 chunks:** chunk **223 carries takeaways 1–3**, **224 carries 4–5**, **230 carries
11–12**; only **6, 7, 8, 9 and 10** get a chunk each.
**`defender.md`, 106 chunks:** chunk **103 opens *"Fourth,"* and chunk 104 opens *"Seventh,"*** — **three
takeaways in one breath.**

⚠️⚠️ **EVERY BRIEF WRITTEN TODAY SAID *"every Key Takeaway is voiced ALONE, in its own `<p>` with a
300 ms break either side."*** **That is TRUE of ` ```facts ` lines and FALSE of Key Takeaways.** **The
agent that caught it stated it as a correction to its own brief rather than working around it.**

### ⚠️ AND THE NUANCE IS THE OPPOSITE OF REASSURING
**The renderer packs BY SIZE.** ✅ **So a SHORT takeaway has neighbours that may qualify it — and a LONG
one does not.** ⚠️⚠️ **Which means the *"voiced alone"* hazard is MOST true exactly where this corpus's
worst takeaways are: the long ones carrying tariff ladders.** **The premise was wrong in the direction
that under-warns about short takeaways and over-warns about nothing.**

✅ **THE OPERATIVE RULE FOR FUTURE BRIEFS:** **say that ` ```facts ` lines ARE voiced alone with a 300 ms
break either side; say that Key Takeaways are PACKED BY SIZE and tell the agent to RENDER AND CHECK
WHICH ONES ARE SOLO.** ⚠️ **A defect in a PACKED takeaway may be rescued by its neighbour; a defect in a
SOLO one is not — and the agent cannot know which without rendering.**

## ✅ THE SCRATCHPAD COLLISION — DIAGNOSED, AND IT IS **NOT** A TOOL DEFECT

**A reviewer reported its *"freshly created and uniquely named"* `--out` dir came back holding SEVEN
rendered document directories.** ✅ **The coordinator re-tested: `md_to_speech.py --only defender --out
<own name>` produced EXACTLY ONE — `positions__defender` — plus `index.json`.**
⚠️⚠️ **SO `--only` RESTRICTS OUTPUT CORRECTLY AND THE TOOL IS FINE. THE DIRECTORY NAME COLLIDED.**
⚠️ **Recording the diagnosis because the wrong one is worse than none: *"the tool renders extra
documents"* would send the next agent chasing a bug that does not exist.** **The remedy is unchanged —
give every concurrent agent its OWN NAMED `--out` subdirectory in the brief, and grep the named
`<layer>__<stem>/` subdirectory rather than the output root.**

## ✅ THE MATCH-PENALTY AFTERMATH, ALL SIX BOOKS — a repair WAS warranted, and it was small

**The previous lane's NHL scoping was honest, but the passage said *"under that book the ejection is not
the end of the matter"* and then named USA Hockey, Hockey Canada and CARHA WITH NO ROUTE ABOVE — so the
implication a reader draws is that under those three it IS the end. It is not, in any of them.**

✅ **THE GENERAL SHAPE THAT IS TRUE: every book that WRITES a match penalty (NHL, PWHL, USA Hockey,
Hockey Canada, CARHA) holds the player out UNTIL THE CASE IS DEALT WITH and makes the report MANDATORY.**
**USA Hockey is the ONLY one whose own book then TARIFFS what follows** — 410(c) makes the process
compulsory, 405(c) bars PRACTICES as well as games, and the Standardized Discipline Policy puts a 627(b)
kick at **Level 3, a RECOMMENDED three-to-five games**, which a hearing *"may reduce, maintain or
increase."* 🔴 **The IIHF is OUTSIDE THE SHAPE ENTIRELY: no match penalty, and NO written interim
suspension — the only two `suspend` hits in the whole book are protective netting and a substitute.**

**The Note reading *"The Referee shall report all incidents pertaining to this rule"* belongs to
**RULE 626, Interference by or with Spectators** — NOT 627.** ⚠️ **The page's RUNNING HEAD reads
*"Kicking Opponent or Puck"*, which is what makes it look like 627's. RULE 627 CARRIES NO NOTE.**
***"A brief that quoted it would have mis-cited."*** ✅ **Nothing mechanical catches this.**
✅ **Also chased: CARHA's *"See also Rule 87"* is *Unnecessary Nuisance* — it prices REFUSING TO LEAVE
after a match penalty, not the act.**

   *"DEALT WITH"*, which is broader — a case can be dealt with without a hearing.** ⚠️ ***"Heard"* implies
   a hearing MUST happen and so implies a LONGER suspension than the books write.** ✅ **Changed in all

2. **It cited only NHL 21.2 while claiming the report is mandatory. 21.3 is the reporting rule.**

## 🔴 `md_to_speech.py` VOICES `CAN/CSA` AS "CAN **OR** CSA" — diagnosed at the source, 26 September 2026

⚠️ **DO NOT CHANGE THE TOOL WHILE A WAVE IS LIVE — recorded, not fixed.** A shared tool is shared state,
and a checker that changes its output mid-round invalidates every finding that rests on it.

**Reproduced through the real renderer, not inferred:**
```
'CAN/CSA Z262.2'   -> 'CAN or CSA <say-as>Z</say-as> two hundred and sixty-two point two'
'CAN/BNQ 9415-370' -> '<say-as>CAN</say-as> slash <say-as>BNQ</say-as> nine four one five dash three seven zero'
```
**Cause: `STANDARDS_BODIES` (`md_to_speech.py`, near the `_standards_code` handler) is
`('CAN/BNQ', 'ISO/DIS', 'ISO/IEC', 'ISO', 'BNQ', 'CSA', 'ASTM', 'NOCSAE')` — `CAN/CSA` IS NOT IN IT**,
so the general slash rule fires and voices the solidus as *"or"*.

⚠️⚠️ **AND ADDING `CAN/CSA` TO THE TUPLE IS HALF A FIX. The pattern requires `\s?\d+` after the body,
so a LETTER-PREFIXED code does not match:** `'CAN/BNQ Z262.2'` also renders *"CAN or BNQ… two hundred and
sixty-two point two"*. **The number would still be spoken as a QUANTITY rather than digit by digit —
which `_standards_code`'s own docstring says is the thing to avoid, because *"a listener writing the code
down needs them"*.** **Two changes, not one.**

⚠️ **The characters in the document MUST NOT CHANGE — `CAN/CSA Z262.2` is a literal published
identifier.** **The repair is the renderer or a rephrase, never a substitution in `content/`.**
**Live sites: `equipment.md:432`, `:436`, `:847`** — and ⚠️ **`:432` is inside a TABLE, so check whether
the renderer drops it before counting it as a listener defect.**

```
python3 - <<'EOF'
import re,glob,io
frames=re.compile(r'all five|five books|of the five|five of the|these five|all four books|the four books|of the four|four of the|these four', re.I)

EOF

## ❌ THE SECOND "CORPUS-WIDE" ALARM REFUTED BEFORE RECORDING — 26 September 2026

**An agent found a real renderer defect in its OWN draft: `7.1(a), (b) and (c)(ii)` speaks as
*"clause a, clause b, clause **cclause two**"*.** It fixed it by writing the rule number out in full, and
reported: *"almost certainly corpus-wide and I only checked my own two files. A grep for
`\)\([ivx]+\)` across `content/` would find the rest."*

⚠️⚠️ **THAT GREP RETURNS 450 HITS ACROSS 26 DOCUMENTS — AND NONE OF THEM IS THE DEFECT.**

✅ **ISOLATED THE ACTUAL TRIGGER by rendering variants, rather than trusting the pattern:**
```
'Rule 7.1(a), (b) and (c)(ii) apply.'  -> BAD  "clause a, clause b, clause cclause two"
'Rule 7.1(a) and (c)(ii) apply.'       -> BAD
'Rule 7.1(b) and 7.1(c)(ii) apply.'    -> ok   "clause b and seven point one, clause c, sub-clause two"
'Rule 7.1(c)(ii) applies.'             -> ok
'Rules 8.3(a)(ii) and 11.1(d)(i)'      -> ok
```
**The mangle needs a CONTINUATION ENUMERATION — bare `(b)` letters trailing a rule number, with the
`(x)(roman)` last. A standalone `N(c)(ii)` is fine.**

✅ **THEN TESTED EMPIRICALLY RATHER THAN BY REGEX — every candidate line pushed through the real
renderer:**
```
lines containing ")(roman)":                286
lines that actually MANGLE in the renderer:   0
```
✅ **The corpus consistently writes the full form, so the shape never occurs. The agent introduced it in
its own draft, caught it, and fixed it.** **Nothing to repair.**

⚠️⚠️ **THIS IS THE SECOND CORPUS-WIDE ALARM REFUTED BEFORE RECORDING TODAY** — the first was
*"CARHA 49(b) appears nowhere in the corpus"* (it appears in five documents). **Both came from careful
agents; both would have sent a wave at a population that does not exist.** ✅ **The discipline that
catches them is the same one this file demands of briefs: A CLAIM ABOUT A POPULATION IS A MEASUREMENT,
AND A MEASUREMENT IS RE-RUN BEFORE IT IS WRITTEN DOWN.** ⚠️ **And a PATTERN COUNT IS NOT A DEFECT COUNT
— 450 candidate hits, 286 renderable lines, 0 defects.**

✅ **KEEP THE RENDERER FACT, WHICH IS REAL AND USEFUL:** **never write a rule citation as a trailing
enumeration ending in a sub-clause** — `7.1(a), (b) and (c)(ii)` — **repeat the rule number instead.**

**PWHL Rule 57 prices interference IN THE NHL'S EXACT WORDS** — *"A player is allowed the ice she is
standing on (body position) and is not required to move in order to let an opponent proceed"* — with
57.2(i) minor, 57.4 discretionary major, 57.5 game misconduct. **So the caption's *"two books"* was
wrong on the numerator as well as the denominator.**

### ⚠️⚠️ AND A "NAME THE ACT, NOT THE RULE" FINDING THE BRIEF DID NOT ANTICIPATE
The caption claims **an ejection is available in every book, only the bar differs**. ✅ **True — but NOT
REACHABLE FROM THE INTERFERENCE RULE IN USA HOCKEY.** **Rule 625 writes ONLY a minor**: 625(a)(1)–(9),
(b) and (c) contain **no major, no game misconduct, no match limb**. **The ejection route is the general
Rule 602(a)** — a match for a player *"who recklessly endangers or attempts to injure any opposing
player"*. ✅ **`breakouts.md`'s own facts block already knows this** (*"602(a)'s match penalty sitting
outside 625 and 640 both"*) — **so caption and host agree, but 625 read alone says the opposite.**
**Written into the module comment as a trap for the next reader.**
